title: Reconfigurable Stream Network Architecture
problem: FPGA-based DNN overlay accelerators suffer from layer-granularity serialization: von Neumann-style coarse-grained ISAs treat each layer instruction atomically, preventing dynamic layer fusion, inter-layer pipelining, and fine-grained bandwidth orchestration across heterogeneous resources (FPGA fabric + AI Engines).
method: RSN (Reconfigurable Stream Network) abstracts the datapath as a circuit-switched network of stateful functional units (FUs) connected by latency-insensitive data streams. Programming a computation means triggering a path through the FU network; multiple non-conflicting paths enable spatial and pipeline parallelism. A three-level instruction decoder fuses multiple FU uOP streams into a single RSN instruction stream with packet-level reuse to minimize instruction overhead (1 byte drives up to 1.6 GFLOPs). RSN-XNN, the prototype on Versal VCK190, virtualizes both FPGA BRAMs/DSPs and AI Engine tiles as heterogeneous FUs through a common stream interface, enabling dynamic sequential layer pipelining and fine-grained DDR/LPDDR bandwidth interleaving during phase transitions.

title: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
problem: Federated Adversarial Training (FAT) requires large models to attain high accuracy and robustness, but memory-constrained edge devices cannot fit full-model training; existing memory-efficient FL methods sacrifice accuracy or robustness through objective inconsistency between local and global models.
method: FedProphet uses adversarial cascade learning: the full model is split into small sequential modules, each trained on one class of devices. Strong convexity regularization on each module's loss ensures local module objectives remain consistent with the global adversarial loss. A server-side coordinator performs Adaptive Perturbation Adjustment (APA) to balance utility vs. robustness trade-off dynamically, and Differentiated Module Assignment (DMA) to assign modules to heterogeneous devices, mitigating objective inconsistency across rounds.

title: FlexInfer: A Flexible CPU-GPU Collaborative Framework for DNN Inference
problem: LLM inference on commodity servers with limited GPU memory forces weight offloading to CPU, but existing offloading systems (FlexGen, SplitGen) use static policies that either underutilize the GPU or overspend PCIe bandwidth on unnecessary transfers.
method: FlexInfer employs an analytical policy estimator that, given current hardware state (GPU memory available, PCIe bandwidth, CPU compute), selects per-layer execution policy: CPU-only, GPU-offload, or SplitGen (split computation between CPU and GPU). Policy decisions are made at runtime without profiling overhead.

title: Fat-Tree QRAM: A High-Bandwidth Shared Quantum Random Access Memory for Parallel Queries
problem: Existing Quantum Random Access Memory (QRAM) architectures, particularly Bucket-Brigade (BB) QRAM, cannot process multiple queries in parallel because the binary tree root node is exclusively occupied for the entire duration of each query, forcing all queries to queue and execute sequentially. In a shared memory system with multiple QPUs, this causes total query latency to scale as O(p*log(N)) for p parallel processes, bottlenecking parallel quantum algorithms.
method: Fat-Tree QRAM replaces each single router node in the BB QRAM binary tree with a Fat-Tree node containing multiple router copies: the router at level i is duplicated (log(N)-i-1) times, so the root contains log(N) router copies and the leaves contain one (matching BB QRAM). This doubling of total router count (from N to 2N-2-log(N)) enables O(log(N)) independent queries to be pipelined simultaneously. Each query is realized via alternating gate steps (CSWAP address loading, 4 circuit layers each) and swap steps (local intra-node SWAP gates, 1 layer each, constant depth because swaps are nearest-neighbor within a node). Two local swap types (SWAP-I and SWAP-II, alternating even/odd router indices) cycle queries through sub-component QRAMs of increasing size without inter-node communication. Hardware is implemented in both modular (superconducting coaxial-cable-linked chips) and on-chip (bi-planar thickness-2 chip with TSVs for inter-plane connections) formats using superconducting cavities with native CSWAP gates. A FIFO scheduling protocol (proven optimal by greedy exchange) maximizes utilization.

title: Garibaldi: A Pairwise Instruction-Data Management for Enhancing Shared Last-Level Cache Performance in Server Workloads
problem: Server workloads suffer from a 'instruction victim' problem in the shared LLC: cold instruction cachelines are evicted by competing hot data cachelines, yet each instruction miss stalls the CPU frontend regardless of how much hot data is already resident in the LLC. Existing LLC management policies (Mockingjay, Hawkeye, DRRIP) optimize for data reuse distance and ignore the cost asymmetry between instruction and data misses.
method: Garibaldi introduces a pairwise instruction-data LLC management scheme built on three mechanisms: (1) a pair table (16K direct-mapped entries, 194 KB total) that tracks each instruction physical address alongside the hotness (miss_cost counter, 6-bit saturating) of the data cachelines it triggers; (2) a selective instruction protection policy using a query-based selection (QBS) mechanism that, at eviction time, queries the pair table and overrides the replacement policy to retain any instruction line whose aged miss_cost exceeds a dynamically adjusted threshold; (3) a pairwise prefetch that, upon serving an unprotected instruction miss, proactively issues prefetch requests for the associated cold data lines recorded in the pair table. Dynamic threshold adjustment uses a synchronized l-bit coloring timer that tracks P(D_miss | I_miss) every 100K LLC accesses and raises or lowers the protection threshold accordingly.
